project-charter.title: 1. Engineering Problem Charter: High-Speed Helical Gearbox

cards.title: Industrial Situation & Transmission Brief
cards.body: A high-speed centrifugal compressor drive in an industrial chemical plant requires an enclosed helical reduction gearbox. The drive motor supplies P = 15.0 kW at N1 = 1440 rpm, and the output compressor shaft operates at N2 = 480 rpm (transmission ratio i = 3.0). Initial trial geometry uses 18 pinion teeth, 54 gear teeth, normal module mn = 4.0 mm, face width b = 40.0 mm, and helix angle psi = 20 deg. The gearbox must satisfy an operational factor of safety [FOS] >= 1.50 under continuous service.

cards.title: Design Specifications & Material Properties
cards.body:
The engineering team has supplied the following design exercise parameters:
• Pinion Material: 40Ni2Cr1Mo28 alloy steel (Sut1 = 800 MPa, Surface Hardness = 350 BHN)
• Gear Material: 55C8 plain carbon steel (Sut2 = 600 MPa, Surface Hardness = 250 BHN)
• Application Service Factor: Ka = 1.25
• Load Concentration Factor: Km = 1.30
• Normal Pressure Angle: alpha_n = 20 deg (full-depth involute)
• Target Safety Factor: [FOS] = 1.50

cards.title: Engineering Responsibility & Failure Consequences
cards.body: High-speed helical gear sets operate under dynamic contact and bending fatigue. Tooth breakage causes catastrophic machine shutdown, while surface pitting results in progressive vibration, severe tooth profile degradation, and gearbox seizure. The engineer must rigorously evaluate both beam strength (Lewis) and wear durability (Buckingham).

gear-geometry.title: 3. Gear Geometry & Transmission Parameters
gear-geometry.description: Calculate transmitted torque, transmission ratio, formative virtual teeth, Lewis form factors, pitch circle diameters, and centre distance.
given: Pinion Teeth: z1 = 18, Gear Teeth: z2 = 54

formulas.name: Virtual Teeth (z')
formulas.formula: z1' = z1 / cos^3(psi), z2' = z2 / cos^3(psi)

formulas.name: Pitch Circle Diameters
formulas.formula: d1 = (z1 * mn) / cos(psi), d2 = (z2 * mn) / cos(psi) [mm]

material-selection.title: 4. Material Selection & Gear-Tooth Failure Evaluation
material-selection.prompt: Evaluate permissible bending stresses and beam strength indices for the pinion and gear to determine the weaker element governing bending design.
material-selection.description: Calculate permissible bending stresses (sigma_b = Sut / 3) and evaluate the strength product (sigma_b * Yv) for both elements.
given: Pinion Material: 40Ni2Cr1Mo28 alloy steel (Sut1 = 800 MPa, 350 BHN)
Gear Material: 55C8 plain carbon steel (Sut2 = 600 MPa, 250 BHN)

mcq.question: Based on the comparative beam strength products, which element is weaker in bending and must govern beam strength calculation?
